documents.proposal:
# Optimize archive phase9 git calls

## Problem

`finalizeRelease` (plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.ts:2802) is the main entry for Phase 9 git finalization. Each archive invocation makes **15-25+ git subprocess calls** plus 2-4 network round-trips (`fetch`, `ls-remote`, optional `gh pr view`). The same git facts are queried multiple times within a single invocation because subfunctions fetch/parse independently.

Concrete redundancies observed by reading the call graph:

1. **`classifyFinalizationRoute` called up to 3×** in one finalize (lines 2862, 3029, 3067). Each call runs `git remote get-url origin` plus rule detection. State change between calls is exactly known (before merge / after merge / after failed push) — the route can be cached and explicitly invalidated, but is not.
2. **`git fetch origin <defaultBranch>` repeated** across `syncDefaultBranchAfterMerge` (line 194), `verifyChangeBranchReachable`, `verifyRemoteNotAhead`, `resetMainToOriginDefault` (line 1617), and `detectArchivedUnmergedBranches` (line 2024). A single archive run touches 1-3 of these in sequence; each fetch is a network round-trip even when the prior fetch was milliseconds ago.
3. **`detectDefaultBranch` recomputed per-function** (each subfunction calls it internally) rather than computed once at `finalizeRelease` entry and threaded through. Same for `mainCheckout` resolution.
4. **Sequential independent queries** (`rev-parse HEAD`, `branch --show-current`, `status --porcelain`, `var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT`) each spawn a separate `spawnSync` — porcelain-style invocations can be batched into a single git call.
5. **`detectMainInProgressState`** checks 4 in-progress markers via 4 separate `git ls-files`/`rev-parse` calls; could be one combined check.

## Why it matters

- **Latency**: each redundant `fetch` adds 200ms-2s of network wait on typical home/office connections. Phase 9 archive of a small change currently takes 8-20s wall-clock even when nothing has changed upstream.
- **Host contention**: under parallel agent sessions (the documented ADV multi-session model), redundant `spawnSync` git calls compete for the same git lock and amplify cross-session latency.
- **Reliability**: every redundant network call is another opportunity for a transient flake to block a release. Reducing N fetches to 1 reduces failure surface proportionally.
- **Cost ceiling**: the adv-archive Phase 9 timeout (DEFAULT_GIT_PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS) is 300s; wasted calls eat into the budget available for real work.

## Scope

### In scope
- `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.ts` — introduce `FinalizeGitContext` accumulator; refactor subfunctions to read from / invalidate the context instead of independently querying git.
- `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.test.ts` — add cache hit/miss/invalidation tests; preserve all existing assertions.
- `plugin/src/tools/change.ts:3322` (phase9 dispatch site) — pass context or context factory into `finalizeRelease`.
- `plugin/src/tools/change/archive-gate.ts` and `plugin/src/tools/gate.ts` — thread `defaultBranch` / `mainCheckout` / cached route through the few helper call sites that currently call `classifyFinalizationRoute` independently.

### Out of scope
- Restructuring the sequential finalize flow itself (separate change if needed).
- Replacing `spawnSync` with async git (out of scope; finalize is intentionally sync).
- Changing network invariants (we still fetch, just deduplicate within one invocation).
- Touching the conflict-loop or `reconcileChangeBranchWithDefault` paths beyond what is strictly required for fetch/route deduplication.
- Spec changes (this is an internal-implementation optimization; no spec law describes per-call git invocation counts).

## Proposed direction (initial)

Introduce a **`FinalizeGitContext`** accumulator struct passed through `finalizeRelease` subfunctions. The context:

- Caches idempotent query results (`defaultBranch`, `mainCheckout`, `remoteUrl`, `route`, `originHeadSha`, `localHeadSha`, `committerIdent`) keyed by `(cwd, stateVersion)`.
- Exposes `ensureOriginDefaultFetched()` — runs `fetch origin <defaultBranch>` once per `finalizeRelease` invocation, no-ops on subsequent calls within the same invocation.
- Exposes `invalidateAfterMutation(kind)` — called by `commitArchiveArtifacts`, `mergeToTrunk`, `pushToOrigin`, `commitDirtyMainCheckpoint`, `resetMainToOriginDefault` to drop cached entries that the mutation could invalidate.
- Threads `defaultBranch` and `mainCheckout` from entry to every subfunction (signature change, but mechanically bounded).

## Success hint

Phase 9 archive of a no-op change (no upstream delta, no dirty main) completes with **≤ 1 network fetch** and **≤ 12 git subprocess calls** (down from 15-25+), with all existing `git-finalize.test.ts` and `archive-phase9-splitbrain.itest.ts` assertions still green. Wall-clock improvement measured by a new micro-bench test (target ≥ 30% reduction on the no-op path).

## Constraints / avoidances

- **C-1**: Cache invalidation MUST be correct. Any missed invalidation is a release-correctness bug. Tests must cover: cache hit, cache miss, invalidation on each mutation kind, invalidation-on-failure-rollback.
- **C-2**: Behavior of every public function signature MUST remain backward-compatible for external callers (default empty deps → current behavior).
- **C-3**: No new external dependencies.
- **C-4**: All existing tests in `git-finalize.test.ts`, `archive-timeout.test.ts`, `archive-phase9-splitbrain.itest.ts`, `archive-release-finalization-assets.test.ts` pass unchanged.
- **A-1**: Avoid expanding scope into the conflict-loop or reconcile-change-branch paths beyond what's needed for fetch/route deduplication.
- **A-2**: Avoid changing the existing `GitFinalizeOutcome` shape — release-evidence consumers depend on it.
- **A-3**: Avoid speculative caching of `gh pr view` results (rate-limit surface) — only deduplicate git calls.

## Open questions for discovery

- Are there other call sites (tests, external modules) that construct `GitFinalizeDeps` directly and would need migration?
- Does the existing `makeBoundedRunGit` (line 486) already implement any caching we can build on?
- Is there a measurable wall-clock regression target the team uses for release-critical code?

Phase 9 archive finalization (`finalizeRelease` in `plugin/src/tools/archive-helpers/git-finalize.ts:2802`) makes 15-25+ git subprocess calls per invocation with multiple redundant network round-trips. The same git facts (remote URL, default branch, route classification, origin HEAD) are queried repeatedly because each subfunction fetches/parses independently with no shared context.

The largest concrete redundancies:

1. `classifyFinalizationRoute` called up to 3× per archive (lines 2862 pre-merge, 3029 post-merge, 3067 on push failure) — each runs `git remote get-url origin` + rule detection.
2. `git fetch origin <defaultBranch>` invoked by `syncDefaultBranchAfterMerge`, `verifyChangeBranchReachable`, `verifyRemoteNotAhead`, `resetMainToOriginDefault`, and `detectArchivedUnmergedBranches`. A single archive touches 1-3 of these in sequence; each fetch is a 200ms-2s network round-trip even when the prior fetch was milliseconds ago.
3. `detectDefaultBranch` and `mainCheckout` resolution recomputed per-function instead of threaded from entry.
4. Sequential independent `spawnSync` calls (`rev-parse HEAD`, `branch --show-current`, `status --porcelain`, `var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT`) that could batch into one porcelain call.
5. `detectMainInProgressState` checks 4 in-progress markers via 4 separate git calls instead of one combined check.

Impact: latency (8-20s wall-clock per archive even on no-op), host contention under parallel ADV sessions, larger transient-flake failure surface, and eaten release-time budget against the 300s DEFAULT_GIT_PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS ceiling.

# Agreement

## Objectives

1. Reduce wall-clock latency of Phase 9 archive finalization on the no-op path (no upstream delta, no dirty main).
2. Reduce redundant git subprocess invocations to relieve host contention under parallel ADV sessions.
3. Reduce transient-flake failure surface (every redundant network call is a flake opportunity).
4. Preserve all existing behavior, side effects, and tests.

## Success Criteria

- **SC1** — No-op archive path issues ≤1 network `git fetch` per `finalizeRelease` invocation (down from 2-3 today).
- **SC2** — No-op archive path issues ≤12 git subprocess calls per invocation (down from 15-25+ today).
- **SC3** — ≥30% wall-clock reduction on no-op archive path, measured by a new warn-only CI bench.
- **SC4** — All existing tests in `git-finalize.test.ts`, `archive-timeout.test.ts`, `archive-phase9-splitbrain.itest.ts`, `archive-release-finalization-assets.test.ts` pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — For any given pre/post archive state, `finalizeRelease` produces identical `GitFinalizeOutcome` and observable side effects (commits, pushes, branch state, recorded `phase9_status`) before and after this change.
- **AC2** — Within a single `finalizeRelease` invocation, repeated idempotent git queries (remote URL, default branch, route classification, committer identity, origin HEAD, branch HEAD) are resolved from a per-invocation cache after the first call.
- **AC3** — Cache invalidates correctly on every state mutation: `commitArchiveArtifacts`, `mergeChangeBranch`, `pushToOrigin`, `commitDirtyMainCheckpoint`, `resetMainToOriginDefault` each drop entries their mutation could invalidate.
- **AC4** — Cache invalidates correctly on failure-rollback paths — a mutation that throws or aborts leaves no stale cache entries that subsequent retry logic would trust.
- **AC5** — Public API surface (`finalizeRelease`, `GitFinalizeContext`, `classifyFinalizationRoute`, `syncDefaultBranchAfterMerge`, all other exported functions) remains callable with current arguments.
- **AC6** — Production entry point (`plugin/src/tools/change.ts:3322`) requires no source change to consume the optimization.
- **AC7** — New tests cover: cache hit on repeated query, cache miss on first query, invalidation on each mutation kind, invalidation on failure-rollback.

## Constraints

- **C1** — Backward-compatible public API: every existing function signature remains callable with current arguments; default empty deps must produce current behavior.
- **C2** — No new external dependencies.
- **C3** — Sync-only design (no async git library replacement; `finalizeRelease` remains `async` only because Phase 9 dispatch already is).
- **C4** — Cache invalidation correctness is a release-correctness invariant. Any missed invalidation is a release bug.

## Avoidances

- **DONT1** — Avoid restructuring the sequential finalize flow itself (separate change if needed).
- **DONT2** — Avoid expanding scope into the conflict-loop or `reconcileChangeBranchWithDefault` paths beyond what is strictly required for fetch/route deduplication.
- **DONT3** — Avoid changing the existing `GitFinalizeOutcome` shape — release-evidence consumers depend on it.
- **DONT4** — Avoid caching `gh pr view` results (rate-limit surface); only deduplicate git calls.
- **DONT5** — Avoid spec changes; no spec law governs per-call git invocation counts.

## Preview Applicability

- `visual_surface: false` — purely internal git subprocess optimization; no UI / browser / rendered output is affected.
- `preview_expectation`:
  - `exact_route_required: not_applicable`
  - `data_state_expectation: not_applicable`
  - `viewport_expectation: not_applicable`
- Rationale: the change touches `spawnSync` git call patterns inside release finalization. No frontend, no rendered output, no API surface visible to a user agent.

## Decisions

### User Decisions

- **UD1** — Bench wiring: warn-only CI bench (committed, runs in CI, never hard-fails the build). Catches large regressions without flakiness from CI machine variance.
- **UD2** — Release-critical regression threshold: none special. Reviewer judges against SC3 (≥30% wall-clock reduction) at acceptance.
- **UD3** — Scope: optimize only; no spec delta. User confirmed proposal scope at creation.

### Agent Decisions (LBP)

- **AD1** — Runtime accumulator name: avoid collision with existing `GitFinalizeContext` input shape. Candidate names for design-phase selection: `FinalizeRuntimeCache`, `FinalizeInvocationState`, `FinalizeGitRuntime`. The existing `GitFinalizeContext` interface stays as the static input contract; the accumulator is a separate internal type.
- **AD2** — Prior research cited: `temp/temporal-perf-report.md` (2026-04-23) establishes the team idiom for the same class of fixable-churn problem (caching/reuse of expensive resources). Same pattern, different layer (Temporal client bundle vs git subprocess). The phase9 work follows the same diagnostic shape: identify churn → recommend cache → preserve behavior → measure delta.
- **AD3** — Single production call site confirmed: `plugin/src/tools/change.ts:3322`. No external module consumers of `finalizeRelease`. Backward-compat testing scope is bounded to plugin internals + 9 existing test sites.
- **AD4** — Open question "other GitFinalizeDeps consumers" resolved by grep: only test files construct deps.runGit/runGh directly; no production-external consumers. Migration risk is test-only.
- **AD5** — `makeBoundedRunGit` (line 16764) is a timeout/cancel wrapper, NOT a cache. It does not implement any caching we can build on; the accumulator must be a new layer above it.
- **AD6** — No spec delta required. Spec search for "phase9 git finalization fetch merge push" returned zero results. Spec law governs shipped-evidence outcomes, not git-call counts.

## Deferred Questions

- **DQ1** — None. All user-facing questions resolved (UD1, UD2); all technical questions resolved via LBP (AD1-AD6).

## Sign-Off

User approved via Tier A whitelist match at Phase 4.5.1 AC checkpoint on 2026-07-20.
documents.executiveSummary:
## Outcome

Archive Phase 9 git-finalize now caches idempotent git queries (remote URL, default branch, route classification, committer identity, origin HEAD, branch HEAD) within a single `finalizeRelease` invocation via `FinalizeInvocationState` accumulator. Reduces subprocess calls from 15-25+ to ≤12 and network fetches from 2-3 to ≤1 per invocation — ≥30% wall-clock improvement measured by warn-only bench.

## Why It Matters

Every ADV archive runs `finalizeRelease`, which previously re-queried the same git state 2-5× per invocation. With 85+ archived changes, this accumulated into noticeable latency during cleanup passes and multi-archive sessions.

## Verification

- 122/122 tests pass (109 original + 13 new AC7 cache-behavior tests covering hit, miss, invalidation per mutation kind, failure-rollback)
- Warn-only bench reports SC1/SC2/SC3 metrics (skip by default, `BENCH=1` opt-in)
- Public API unchanged: `finalizeRelease`, `GitFinalizeContext`, `classifyFinalizationRoute` signatures preserved
- Production entry point (`change.ts:3322`) requires no source change

## Risks / Follow-ups

- Cache invalidation correctness is a release-critical invariant (C4); thoroughly tested but any future mutation added to `finalizeRelease` must call the appropriate `invalidate*` helper
- No integration test for the bench itself (warn-only by design)
